title: An agent is a loop where the model picks each step, and your code owns every exit
aria: Billpod's assistant as an agent loop. Code checks the limits, the model picks the next tool call, and a reply with no tool call ends the loop. Each tool call is a proposal: unknown names get an error result, reads run at once, and a change is checked against the stored bill, then sealed into a 10-minute token while the person sees a card. The approval is a second HTTP request that runs only the sealed call once and carries the step count on. A bottom row compares a workflow, an agent at about 4 times a chat's tokens and a multi-agent system at about 15 times.

build.title: Code checks the limits, then asks the model
build.text: Before each model call the loop checks: at most 6 calls per request, 60 s per step, 2048 output tokens. Each call resends the whole transcript, so each costs more than the last.

build.title: One built-in exit, the rest are yours
build.text: A reply with no tool call is the only exit the model gives. Your code adds the rest: LOOP_LIMIT after 6 calls, stop when the person leaves, AI_FAILED on a blocked reply. There is no money cap and no deadline.

build.title: Every tool call is a proposal
build.text: An unknown name gets an UNKNOWN_TOOL result. A read runs at once and its result goes into the next call. A change is checked against the stored bill and its version.

build.title: A change pauses the turn
build.text: A change that passes is sealed with the transcript, the results and the count into an AES-256-GCM token for 10 minutes. The person sees a card, and the request ends with nothing written.

build.title: The approval resumes once
build.text: Approve is a second HTTP request. It claims the card id once (a 2nd click gets 409), runs only the sealed call and carries the count on. It never gets a fresh 6.

build.title: Use a workflow when you can
build.text: An agent uses about 4 times a chat's tokens, a multi-agent system about 15 times. When you can draw the flowchart, let your code fix the order of calls.

route.title: Check the cap, then ask the model
route.text: Model call 1 of 6. The loop sends the system prompt, the conversation and the tool list. The model cannot run anything: it replies with a tool call, find_bills “electricity”.

route.title: Run the read at once and send everything back
route.text: find_bills runs straight away and returns bill b42, version 3 (example). The model remembers nothing, so call 2 resends call 1, its reply and the result. Every call id gets a result.

route.title: Check the write against stored data before showing it
route.text: The model asks for `mark_paid` b42, version 3. A tool call is only a proposal: it must be on the allow-list, match its schema, name a bill in this household and carry the version the model read.

route.title: Save the paused loop and end the request
route.text: Marking a bill paid needs the person's yes. The loop seals the transcript, the results, the call count and the checked arguments into a 10-minute AES-256-GCM token, shows a card, and the request ends. Nothing is written yet.

route.title: Resume once and run exactly what was checked
route.text: Approve sends the token in a second request. The token works once, so a second click gets 409. The loop runs the sealed arguments only, and 2 of the 6 model calls are already used.

route.title: Stop when a reply has no tool call
route.text: Call 3 asks for list_due. Call 4 answers in plain text: “Done. Still due: water, 48.20”. That is 4 of 6 calls across two HTTP requests, and no code wrote the order of steps.
